newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates remain steady, seen down.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates remain steady, seen down.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates were steady on Thursday on select buying by mills amid a shortage of ready stocks, but would drop in next couple of weeks when the arrival of new crop picks up, dealers said.

"For the time being, the rates are steady, but they will drop after the arrival of new supplies increases from July 15 to August 1," dealer Mustafa Hussain said. "Compared to last year, this year mills are hit by financial problems and they can only be buyers at lower levels."
He said most of the deals for stocks from the old 1996/97 were being done on credit.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was quoted around 2,250 ($55.47) rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
